chunks: Hadith 3203 — In the narration of Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from his father, he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me:

"O Sadīr, do you visit the grave of al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام every day?" I said, "May I be your ransom, no." He said, "How neglectful you are! Then do you visit him every month?" I said, "No." He said, "Then do you visit him every year?" I said, "That may sometimes happen."

He said, "O Sadīr, how neglectful you are toward al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام. Do you not know that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has a thousand thousand angels, disheveled and dust-covered, who weep and visit, and do not cease? And what would it cost you, O Sadīr, to visit the grave of al-Ḥusayn صلى الله عليه وآله in every Friday five times, or once every day?"

I said, "May I be your ransom, there are many farsakhs between us and him." So he said to me, "Go up onto your roof, then turn right and left, then raise your head to the sky, then incline toward the grave and say: 'Peace be upon you, O Abā ʿAbdillāh. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' By that, a visitation will be written for you, and the visitation is a hajj and an ʿumrah."
Sadīr said: Sometimes I did that more than twenty times in a month.

key_terms.السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ: the formula of greeting and salutation directed in ziyārah
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ: Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, the object of visitation in this narration
key_terms.تَزُورُ: to visit in the devotional sense of performing ziyārah
key_terms.حَجَّةٌ: a hajj in reward and spiritual equivalence as stated in the narration
key_terms.زَوْرَةٌ: a single act of visitation recorded for the visitor
key_terms.عُمْرَةٌ: an ʿumrah in reward and spiritual equivalence as stated in the narration
key_terms.قَبْرَ: the grave or resting place being visited
key_terms.مَلَكٍ: an angel, referring here to the heavenly beings who weep and visit

ai.seo_question: How can someone perform ziyārah of Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام from a distance?
ai.summary: This hadith strongly encourages the ziyārah of Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, even for those unable to travel to his grave because of distance. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teaches that sending salām toward the grave from afar is counted as a visitation, and he emphasizes the continual mourning and visitation of the angels for al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3203 - In a narration from Hanan ibn Sadeer from his father, he said: Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said to me:

"O Sadeer, do you visit the grave of al-Husayn (as) every day?"
I said: "May I be your ransom, no."
Imam (as) said: "How distant you are! Do you visit it every month?"
I said: "No."
Imam (as) said: "Do you visit it every year?"
I said: "It may happen."

Imam (as) said: "O Sadeer, how neglectful you are toward al-Husayn (as), peace be upon him. Do you not know that Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, has a thousand thousand angels, disheveled and covered in dust, who cry and visit him without ceasing? What would it harm you, O Sadeer, to visit the grave of al-Husayn (as) five times every Friday or once every day?"

I said: "May I be your ransom, there are many leagues between us and his grave."
Imam (as) said to me: "Ascend to the roof of your house, turn right and left, then lift your head toward the sky, incline toward the direction of his grave, and say:
'Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdullah. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His blessings.'
It will be written for you as a visitation, and each visitation is equal to a Hajj and an Umrah."
Sadeer said: "Sometimes I did this more than twenty times in a month."
